plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil, and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated in gardens and for essential oil production.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence are often at peak bloom around the summer solstice, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since Romans used it in their baths.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flowers above broad, glossy green leaves. It prefers partial shade and moist, rich soil, and is popular in cottage gardens and along coastlines.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early autumn (June to September)
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely cultivated in temperate regions including the eastern United States, the UK, the Azores, and Western Europe
plants.funFact: The flower color depends on soil pH: acidic soils with available aluminum produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: A hardy aquatic perennial with large round floating leaves and fragrant, star-shaped flowers that float on the surface of still or slow-moving fresh water. The blooms open in the morning and close in the afternoon.
plants.location: Lakes, ponds, and slow rivers across Europe, North Africa, and parts of western Asia
plants.funFact: The flower stalks can lengthen or shorten to follow changes in water depth, and after pollination the stem coils downward to ripen seeds underwater.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, made of showy bracts surrounding a central cone of true flowers. It grows in fynbos vegetation and is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and periodic fires.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from about May to September, so it is in bloom around the June solstice
plants.location: Southwestern and southern Cape regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its lineage is ancient: Proteas existed before the supercontinent Gondwana broke apart.
